updates.note: Urged applicants to log in and verify bank details before Thanksgiving; said FEMA never charges a fee and never calls asking for a password.
Service piece: how to check FEMA deposit details.

Announced 410 accounts taken over after about 220,000 automated login attempts with passwords stolen elsewhere; extra verification added; 'If your account was one of them, you will be repaid.' FEMA did not say amount or who was behind it.
Broke FEMA's 410-account announcement for Harborline 6.
Said every affected applicant will be repaid; declined to discuss who might be responsible or how much was diverted.

Called the attack credential stuffing; noted fewer than two in every thousand attempts worked; declined to guess who was behind it ('That's for investigators to say'); advice: unique passwords, second sign-in step, secure email first.
Reported the FEMA account takeover totals and timeline for the Ledger.

Explained credential stuffing in three steps for a national audience; success rate about two-tenths of 1 percent; 'that's a habit, not a patch'; declined to speculate on who was behind it ('That's for the government to say').
National explainer on credential stuffing against hurricane aid accounts.
Thanksgiving message thanking the station community for coming back and helping others.
Thanksgiving: depot workers restored the mission after returning to flooded hangars, many while repairing their own homes.
Thanksgiving feature for station and depot families.

Hosted Thanksgiving meal at the fellowship hall; line reached the corner by 10 a.m.; volunteers helping neighbors without smartphones apply and check deposit details. Lines: 'The storm is over for some people. It's not over here.' 'Half my people don't have an email address.' Said hub stays open through Christmas.
Thanksgiving scene at Whitfield's relief hub.

Black Friday: selling bait from coolers on the porch of his gutted shop while a carpenter works inside; plywood sign 'LIVE SHRIMP. CHEAP ADVICE. NO REFUNDS ON EITHER.'; hopes walls closed in by Christmas. Lines: 'Big ships don't buy bait.' 'I invented island time.'
Black Friday small-business feature from Port Aransas.

Boat tied up at Aransas Pass; fished zero days in the bay in ten weeks; filed spill damage claim two days after the process opened (Nov. 18) with a grocery bag of fuel receipts and his father's-style logbooks. Lines: 'a boat that doesn't move is just an expensive house for pelicans'; 'They want numbers, I have numbers. What I don't have is a paycheck.'
Said the bay closure stays until the science supports lifting it; urged fishers to keep records and file claims.
Feature on bay closure and fishers' claims.

Announced the Navy suspended Quellmar Fuel Partners pending a fuel quality review linked to the October generator failure; 'we're not going to get ahead of the review'; declined to discuss duration or supply arrangements, citing security.
Disputed the suspension: 'All product we delivered meets specifications'; said Quellmar stepped up when the regular supplier flooded and would cooperate.
Reported the Navy's suspension of Quellmar.
Second-wave post quoted to debunk: 'THEY GOT RICH OFF OUR STORM. Contractors are STEALING your aid and nobody will say it.' No evidence offered.
Rumor control: 'Ask us about any contract. The records are public'; 'A made-up number doesn't hold anybody accountable.'
Fact-checked the first contractor-rumor claims: $140 million debris contract (false; $14.2M) and FEMA stopped paying families (false).
Giving Tuesday advice: 'Stuff is heavy. Money moves at the speed of light'; give cash and boring essentials (diapers, cleaning supplies, grocery cards) to local groups.
Giving Tuesday service piece.
Disputed the Navy suspension Monday: 'Every load we delivered met specifications, and we have the paperwork to show it'; disappointed, cooperating, expects to be cleared.
'The review will determine what happened'; said power on the station is on; declined to discuss backup arrangements.
Explained the fuel quality review and timeline.

Explained why the 'stolen aid' wave spreads: false stories built around something true; 'When people are waiting, any story that explains the wait feels true'; declined to say who is behind the posts ('I don't do attribution by vibes').
Explainer on the second rumor wave and sorting real questions from false claims.

Season-end: odds of another storm this late are very low, but 'the end of the season isn't the end of the storm for anybody still fixing a roof'; urged off-season planning, especially for people without a ride out.
Surge as 'a giant hand pushing the whole bay inland'; marshes recover over seasons and years; wary of anyone giving a date.
Season-end feature on Rafael's lasting footprint.
'The channel is open, and we intend to keep it that way'; port workers 'earned a quiet winter.'
Declined to comment on open investigations; 'Our focus is safe navigation, and the channel is open.'
Season-end channel timeline for the trade.
Column: ask hard questions about storm contracts, don't share fake numbers; noted she has covered two prior hurricanes.
Named in Ledger column as one of the loudest accounts in the 'stolen aid' wave, after spreading the home-seizure rumor in September.
Records investigation published: Vantorra billed about 2.3 times the debris tonnage the county's drone and satellite surveys estimated; requests for payment records pending.
Denied overbilling: 'We bill for what we haul, load by load'; 'Pictures from the sky don't pick up debris. Trucks do.' Invited doubters to 'ride along with one of my trucks. Bring a lunch.'
County had received the Ledger's questions and was looking at the records; would not get ahead of that.
Co-reported the debris billing investigation.
By phone to Harborline 6: 'I've got a ticket for every load'; 'Come count 'em with me.'
TV follow on the Ledger's debris billing report.
Interview Thursday denying overbilling: 'Surveys are guesses. Tickets are facts'; 'I'm not a satellite guy. I'm a trucks guy'; said load records are on file with the county.
Explainer on how debris is counted; has requested load tickets and monitoring records.
Family Q&A: the station has power and keeping it that way is a priority; no action needed by families; will share results when the review is complete.
Statement repeated: all product delivered meets specifications.
Family Q&A on the fuel supplier suspension.
Post seizing on the Ledger report: 'SEE?? We TOLD you. They are stealing YOUR aid.' Debunked: report concerns debris billing, not FEMA household payments.
Second fact-check in the wave: '2.3 times its contract' misleading (tons, not dollars); 'proves contractors stole your FEMA check' false.
Announced payments to Vantorra on hold pending audit: 'That's not a finding of anything. It's us counting before we pay.' Declined to say amount paid, auditor or timeline.
Welcomed the audit: 'Our tickets will speak for themselves'; asked county to move quickly because crews have families to care for at Christmas.
Reported the county's payment pause.
To Harborline 6: 'We're doing the math before we write the next check... this is your money.'
TV report on the payment pause.

Six weeks after the notice lifted, still keeps a case of bottled water by her back door; made Thanksgiving turkey brine with tap water ('That's progress. Next step is the coffee'); wants a plan from the city, 'Not a press release.'
Water meets standards after repairs and testing; apologized for what the fall asked of residents; said the utility would share more about plans as they develop.
Feature on rebuilding trust in tap water, with practical steps.

Walks North Beach at 7 a.m. checking the tide line for oil; smelled the oil before he saw it ('Like somebody left a truck running in your kitchen'); fried a Thanksgiving turkey in a driveway with neighbors; 'Everybody's got a bridge story now.'
'Monitoring isn't walking away. If somebody sees oil, we want to know about it.'
North Beach December feature.

Recovering from broken arm and concussion; arm was in a cast most of November; sleeps with the TV on now; in physical therapy; hopes to be cleared to return to work after the new year; spending holidays with family. 'I'm more scared of sitting on my couch until March.'

Back on the water since mid-November, once the company had a boat for him; trusts the sweep; won't speculate on who did it ('I drive tugs'); holding a spot on his crew for Fontenot; said Fontenot's first question that night was whether everyone else was OK.
Profile of the injured deckhand and his captain.

New details: a window in her duplex hasn't closed fully since the storm ('a heater that heats the street'); landlord hasn't fixed window or stained ceiling; tapes plastic over the window at night; kids call it 'indoor camping.' FEMA application still pending.
General advice for damp homes: clean small mold areas, ventilate, call doctor for asthma; never heat with gas stove, oven or grill (carbon monoxide).
Feature on renters in storm-damaged homes heading into winter.
'There are no findings yet. When there are, you'll hear them from us, not from a meme.'
Third fact-check in the wave: payment pause doesn't freeze FEMA aid; no audit findings released.
Confirmed a federal inspector general opened a review of emergency debris and fuel contracts in the Coastal Bend.
On the IG review: 'We've got nothing to hide. Bring on the reviews.'
On the IG review: 'We'll cooperate fully with any review. All product we delivered meets specifications.'
County will cooperate with federal reviewers: 'Whatever they ask for, they'll get.'
Brief on the IG review.
Q&A explainer distinguishing the IG review, the county audit and the Navy fuel review.
Quoted nationally: county will cooperate with any federal review.
National story on the IG review.
Year-end: 'Two closures in one quarter, from two completely different causes'; 'The question now is confidence, not capacity'; 'An open question is harder to price.'
'The channel is open, and we're moving barrels.'
Year-end crude flows analysis.
Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day week message; fuel review ongoing; referred IG questions to the inspector general.
Depot workers 'spent the fall fixing hangars by day and their own houses at night. We want them to rest.'
Holiday-season weekly for station families.
Profile: still sees the same neighborhoods more than she'd like; volunteered to work Christmas Eve ('somebody who knows where the eye wash is').
Flu season advice: wash hands, stay home when sick, get a flu shot; 'It's not too late.'
Profile of ER charge nurse heading into the holidays.
Investigation remains open; not in a position to discuss it.
Brightwake has not switched remote access back on; rebuilding remote access 'from the ground up, and nothing gets turned back on until we're certain.'
'We are cooperating fully with the Unified Command and with investigators.'
General guidance: operators should know who connects remotely, when and why, and be able to 'shut that door fast.'
Status report on the spill and remote-access probe.
Her Calallen block is stringing Christmas lights on tarp-covered houses; 'It's a contest now. I'm losing'; her students made paper snowflakes for her window; 'It's about saying we're still here.'
Holiday lights feature with safety tips.
Preparing to film the Geminids; hasn't filmed anything like the September lights since; people now send him planes, satellites and Venus; 'I'm careful with the word probably.'
Geminids viewing tips with Jaime Ortega.
Opened a toy table on Dec. 12; 'Nobody's kid should have to learn about hurricanes and Santa Claus in the same year'; 'Remember us in January.'
Picked gifts for her three children at the hub's toy table; 'Este año, Santa viene en autobús'; checks her bank every morning ('Same means nobody took it'); FEMA application still pending.
Community feature on the hub's toy table.

Presented findings with Coastline: low-income surge-zone tracts got aid dollars at about half their share of residents; median 911 response 2.1 times high-income areas. 'Half. Not a little less. Half.' Cautioned it shows who got less, not why in every case.
'We told anybody who would listen. Now it's got a number on it. I hope the number does what my voice couldn't.'
Published the aid-gap analysis with Dr. Sofia Marquez.

Method explainer: per-resident share is 'the simplest fairness test'; welcomes damage-based comparisons; factors worth examining include bridge closures, vehicle and internet access, and how people learned about aid.
Methodology guide to the analysis.
Reacted to the analysis: 'Half? I could have told them that for free'; 'I'm the most patient woman in Texas. Patience doesn't fix a roof.' Application still pending; ceiling still stained.
To the Ledger: 'The number tells you where to look. Now somebody has to go look.'
Ledger follow-up on the equity analysis using Coastline data.
National: 'Disasters don't create inequality. They reveal it, and then they compound it'; suggested bringing registration into neighborhoods.
National wire story on the aid-gap analysis.
'I'm a fisherman who doesn't fish. Ask me in the spring.'
Shop rebuild: 'the drywall's half up, and the pelicans don't care what month it is.'
Co-wrote three-month status roundup.
Co-wrote three-month status roundup.
'We told them in September. We told them in October... I'm not surprised. I'm tired.'
On the bridge closures: 'When the bridges closed, you were on your own'; had neighbors who never tried to call.
Reaction piece on the aid-gap analysis.

Five recommendations: go door to door; put sites on bus lines near trusted hubs; make help human and multilingual; reuse pre-storm evacuation-assistance lists after storms; track equity weekly. 'It's shoe leather.'
Interview on fixes for the aid gap.
Announced door-to-door registration: 'If you can't get to us, we'll come to you... we're going to keep knocking.'
Teams carry federal photo ID and never ask for money or passwords.
Asked teams to start with an 80-year-old neighbor with no phone; 'Then come to mine, and I'll make coffee.' Application still pending.
Reported the door-to-door announcement.
'Our people carry federal photo ID, and they never charge a fee... ask to see the badge, and call the helpline to check.'
Service guide to spotting real registration teams.
Called door-to-door 'the right first step'; declined credit; urged measuring doors, applications and dollars by neighborhood; said 911 findings need their own response before the next storm.
Offered to walk with the teams on day one: 'My door's open, and my list is long.'
Reaction to the door-to-door announcement.
